agents.name: Bob
memories: Water is the constraint that ends farms.
Do not plant more than we can water.

today.why: The new sprout is in and clear sky still pulls three points a day even with the ditch. Water is the constraint that ends farms — better spend eight on wet ground than watch a fresh row dry out.
today.expect: East field moisture back up so the sprout holds through another clear stretch.

yesterday.why: The ear is ripe and dawn still takes two corn no matter how careful we are. Leaving a full row standing while the bin only shrinks is how a careful farm goes hungry.
yesterday.expect: Corn in storage and an empty field before the ration can outrun the crop.

agents.name: Alice
memories: Unused seeds are a delay, not a reserve.
Ditches compound. Heat does not wait.

today.why: We just spent nothing on the cistern while the harvest and reseeding happened. Heat does not wait, and a cistern that sits still while the next soak is coming is a delay dressed as caution.
today.expect: Cistern topped so tomorrow's watering does not borrow from a thin reserve.

yesterday.why: Unused seeds are a delay, not a reserve. The second the ear comes off, the next row goes in — heat does not wait for an empty sack.
yesterday.expect: A seeded row catching tomorrow's moisture while the harvest sits in the bin.
